For channel 0 (agent), all large weights are confined to column 1, the leftmost playable column: e.g. (r2,c1) 7.10, (r1,c1) 6.48, (r7,c1) 5.22, (r6,c1) 4.98, (r8,c1) 4.68. This means the network only cares about the agentâs vertical position along a fixed left-edge column. For channel 1 (moving objects), weights are spread across the inner grid, strongest around columns 2â3 and rows 5â6: (r6,c3) 12.17, (r5,c2) 10.81, (r2,c2) 10.66, (r7,c2) 9.64, (r3,c3) 9.53. This suggests a moving object such as a ball, with the network attending most when it is near the left side. For channel 2 (reward targets), the strongest weights are on the right edge: (r6,c9) 0.97, (r2,c9) 0.85, (r4,c9) 0.82, (r5,c9) 0.82, (r7,c9) 0.81. This points to a reward zone on the right. Channel 3 (obstacles) is high around the border, consistent with walls. Channel 4 (previous frame) is broad, as expected for previous positions of the agent and moving object.

Reasoning: The agent is constrained to a single vertical column on the left, which rules out games where the player moves freely in 2D, such as Snake, Pac-Man, Frogger, or Space Invaders. A bottom paddle game like Breakout would put agent weights along a bottom row, not column 1. A left-side vertical paddle, a moving ball, and a right-side reward/goal zone strongly match Pong. In Pong, the player controls the left paddle, moves up/down to hit the ball, and scores when the ball passes the opponent on the right. Left/right actions would be irrelevant, and the network would learn to ignore them.

Game: Pong

Description: The agent controls a paddle on the left edge, moving up or down to hit a moving ball. Reward is given when the ball reaches the right side, i.e. when the agent successfully scores against the opponent.

Confidence: 92%
